title: Advanced Grammar in an Essay
topic: Should every student have a chance to play in class games, even if some students play better than others?
sentences: School games are part of school life, but some students play better than others.
I claim that every student should have a chance to play.
On the one hand, some students may make more mistakes during games.
If they play, the team will sometimes lose since these mistakes can help the other team.
On the other hand, playing together can help students make friends and feel better.
Some students have felt alone, so joining a team can help them.
In conclusion, I believe that everyone should have a chance to play.
Therefore, every student should be included in class games.
For example, they may pass the ball to the other team.
Moreover, students can learn to help each other when they play together.
paragraphs: School games are part of school life, but some students play better than others. I claim that every student should have a chance to play.

On the one hand, some students may make more mistakes during games. If they play, the team will sometimes lose since these mistakes can help the other team. For example, they may pass the ball to the other team.

On the other hand, playing together can help students make friends and feel better. Some students have felt alone, so joining a team can help them. Moreover, students can learn to help each other when they play together.
In conclusion, I believe that everyone should have a chance to play. Therefore, every student should be included in class games.

slides.title: Welcome
slides.text: Grade 11 · 5-point English
slides.he: Bnei Akiva Yeshiva, Kiryat Herzog
slides.note: Apply grammar already learned. Do not reteach the whole grammar unit.

slides.title: A clear essay, one step at a time
slides.text: Simple words. Clear ideas.
slides.he: Use familiar words and useful sentence patterns.
slides.note: Aim for clear, developed ideas in language students can use independently. This model does not guarantee an exam score.

slides.title: The writing task
slides.text: Should every student have a chance to play in class games, even if some students play better than others?
slides.he: Should everyone have a chance to play?
slides.note: Distinguish class games from selection for a school team. This is a practice task.

slides.title: Four paragraphs
slides.text:
Introduction
On the one hand, ...
On the other hand, ...
In conclusion, ...
slides.he: Opening and opinion; an idea against; an idea for; conclusion.
slides.note: Practice target: 120–140 words. In an exam, follow the task instructions.

slides.title: Useful words for other essays
slides.text:
I claim that ...
since / For example, / Moreover,
Therefore, / In conclusion,
slides.he: Choose a phrase that fits your idea.
slides.note: Since gives a reason. Moreover adds an idea. Therefore gives a result. Reuse a small set of useful phrases.

slides.title: Words for this topic
slides.text:
games / play / team
friends / help / mistakes
slides.he: Choose words you know how to use.
slides.note: Prefer familiar, accurate words such as games, help and friends. A longer word is not automatically better.

slides.title: A short plan
slides.text: One idea against. One idea for.
slides.he: What is one problem? What is one benefit?
slides.note: Write two short notes. First-language notes are fine at this planning stage. Do not write the whole essay yet.

slides.title: First Conditional
slides.text: If + Present Simple, will + verb

slides.title: Patterns for your next essay
slides.text:
If ..., ... will ...
Some ... have ...
... should be ...
slides.he: Change the idea and topic words. Choose a pattern that fits.
slides.note: Do not force a pattern into an unrelated idea. Playing and joining also model gerunds naturally; no separate unit is needed.

slides.title: Your own essay
slides.text: Should teenagers have an after-school job?
slides.he: Choose your opinion and develop your ideas.
slides.note: Keep four paragraphs. Do not show a model for this new topic before students try.

slides.title: Plan your essay
slides.text: My opinion / An idea against / An idea for
slides.he: Write three short notes.
slides.note: Allow three minutes. Help with one idea at a time. Useful words: work, money, time, school, tired, help.

slides.title: Write your essay
slides.text: Write 120–140 words.
slides.he: Four paragraphs. One sentence at a time.
slides.note: Protect 14 minutes of writing. Do not stop the class for each error. Give at most two key corrections per student. An unfinished draft can be completed later.

slides.title: Before you edit
slides.text:
Task / reasons / examples
If ... will / have + V3 / should be + V3
slides.he: Check ideas and four paragraphs first. Then check language.
slides.note: Count words and develop the body if needed. Keep necessary ideas even when simplifying the language.

slides.title: Edit your essay
slides.text: Read your essay. Improve two things.
slides.he: Improve one idea or explanation and one language point.
slides.note: Protect three minutes of editing. Use the phrase bank without automatically replacing correct words.

slides.title: Exit question
slides.text: Which sentence explains how games help?
slides.note: A simple sentence that explains an idea is better than one students cannot understand or use.
options: Games help students make friends since they spend time together.
Games help students since games help students.
